chapter: Los Angeles, Ellington and the recording scene
title: Cafe Society in New York with Lee and Lester's band
summary: Barney Josephson hires the group; the New York eight-to-four hours, Judy Holiday's Reviewers, Pete Johnson and Albert Ammons.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So I guess it was through him that Barney Josephson and Cafe Society heard about us, and hired us to come to New York. This is funny. Out here... This was during the War. Was it? Yeah, during the War. Out here we worked from 10 to 2, four hours a night, which was nice. So we found out we were getting forty or fifty dollars a week more to go to the Cafe Society in New York. But we didn't know that in New York you worked from 8 to 4.

Eight hours! But that was fun. And anyhow, at the Cafe Society Downtown at this time there was a group called the Reviewers. Judy Holiday was a member of the group, who later became a big star. Pete Johnson and Albert Ammons were the two boogie-woogie pianists, and the show also had a Classical pianist, Sam Reichman Lewis he was called. This was, you know, a lot of fun, although the hours were really ridiculous. Because when you'd get off at 4 o'clock in the morning in New York, you know, you'd go out and eat, and it would always be daylight when I'd get home, and consequently it was just one... You know, you'd get enough sleep to come back to work and the same routine. So
from that standpoint, I never did dig working in New York, because the hours are too long.
